page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture Intel Xeon processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz and is equipped with a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports hardware instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance consistently in the average performance tier across most standard workloads. The stress-ng CPU test yields a single-core score of 1828.39 and a multi-core score of 7717.41. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 426.16 GB/sec, which drops to 60.16 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a large block write bandwidth of 42.66 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 9.56 GB/sec and processes 7.81 million Redis SET operations per second. Software compilation with Clang scores 8073.0 on Geekbench, while database operations score 4032.39 on Passmark.

The instance exhibits clear performance limitations when handling larger computational models. While small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model runs efficiently at 732.07 tokens/sec for prompt processing, scaling up to a medium 7B model results in a significant performance drop, yielding a poor 15.99 tokens/sec for prompt processing and a weak 7.29 tokens/sec for text generation. Because it lacks local storage and GPU acceleration, it is not suitable for heavy data storage, high-speed local disk I/O, or complex deep learning tasks. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including moderate web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight text or image processing.

It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, a 33 MB L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard workloads, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5300.0 and a static web serving throughput of 9.56 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weak performance on larger computational tasks, such as medium-sized LLM inference. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced, non-storage-intensive workloads, making it suitable for general-purpose applications, software compilation, Redis deployments, and moderate web serving.
